note: Savings goals, highest priority first. Two kinds: a RATE goal (the common one) simply saves a share of income every month - no target amount, no date, and success is whether the money actually moved. A TARGET goal saves a specific amount by a specific date. Each goal can name the account its contributions land in (account_match), so two goals funded from two accounts are tracked separately.

example_rate_goal.name: Monthly savings
example_rate_goal._note: Save 20% of after-tax income every month. contribution_type can also be 'fixed' with contribution_fixed_cents. No target_cents or target_date needed.

example_target_goal.name: House down payment
example_target_goal._note: Use this only when saving toward a specific sum by a specific date. The report then also reports whether the contribution plan is large enough to reach it in time.
